text:
Marta: Heads up, CI perf run failed on canary deployment after merged PR #1129. p95 decode jumped ~2.4x for short-sequence workloads.
Ryan: saw the alert, digging in. Any recent kernel-selection changes in the merge?
Marta: yes, the merge toggled the kernel selector to prefer fused-attn for < 64 seqs when GPU occupancy low.
Sam: that sounds risky. We only had perf tests for long sequences in that patch.
Ingrid: repro locally on my dev box: run ./tools/loadtest --profile shortseq --batch 8 yields p95 330ms vs 120ms on main.
Ryan: can you paste the profile flamegraph?
Ingrid: pasted: https://internal-grafana/redwood/flame/3789 (private) — top shows a big spike in `fused_attn_forward` vs `optimized_attn`
Sam: if fused_attn is chosen, kernel launch overhead + extra memory copies might dominate at short seqs. selector heuristic probably mis-ranked cost.
Marta: CI-bot posted the perf diff: 
```
Benchmark: decode_shortseq_16
main: p95=118ms
PR-1129: p95=280ms (+137%)
```
Ryan: let's run a quick bisect across commits in the merge. I can try building containers for each commit and run microbench.
Sam: before that, can we force the old kernel via env override and confirm perf returns to normal? set REDW_KERNEL_PREFER=optimized_attn
Ingrid: ran that, p95 back to 125ms. So kernel choice is the root cause.
Marta: good repro. Need fix options: revert selector change, adjust heuristic thresholds, or add a fast-path for shortseq that overrides fused-attn.
Ryan: my vote is heuristic tweak + small guard (don't pick fused-attn when seq<=48 and batch<=8).
Sam: agree. Also add a CI microbench for short sequences so this doesn't regress silently.
Ingrid: opened a hotfix PR #1135 with guard + unit test. PTAL.
Marta: thanks. Can we also hold the canary until the fix lands? CI-bot: Canary flagged; rollout paused due to perf regression.
CI-bot: Canary hold enacted by perf-safety; reason: p95 decode increase on shortseq workloads.
Ryan: I'll run more exhaustive tests (different batch sizes, quant modes) and post traces.
Sam: once PR merged, we should run the full canary perf run and then unpause.
Marta: thanks all — good catch. Follow-up: create an eval case in Redwood Optimize for shortseq patterns.
Ryan: noted, I'll add it to the backlog and assign myself.
Ingrid: linking logs & flamegraphs in the PR.
Sam: small reminder: add a changelog note that kernel selection heuristics changed in that merge so ops teams aren't surprised next time.
Marta: agreed. Closing action items: (1) merge #1135 hotfix, (2) add CI microbench shortseq, (3) update selector tests, (4) unblock canary after perf runs.
Marta: :thumbsup:
